title: Adaptive evidence acquisition for behavioral hypothesis elimination
question: Can adaptive selection of the next observable behavior row reduce candidate ambiguity and exact verification work at a fixed evidence budget, compared with the frozen non-adaptive support order?
hypothesis: A target-identity-blind minimax probe selector should reduce the remaining behavior-compatible candidate set faster than the frozen random support order, especially at large M, improving capability at the same number of observed rows.

arms.name: adaptive_minimax
arms.intervention: greedily choose the unseen row minimizing the worst-case remaining compatible-candidate count using public candidate truth tables and observations acquired so far

arms.name: fixed_random
arms.intervention: use the deterministic support-row permutation already registered in G-CASM-013 without adaptation

endpoints.name: paired_fixed_success_delta_k4_b8
endpoints.role: primary — seed-level paired difference in fixed-budget exact capability at K=4 and B=8

endpoints.name: support_consistent_candidate_count
endpoints.role: secondary — remaining behavioral ambiguity after each probe budget

endpoints.name: unique_candidate_fraction
endpoints.role: secondary — fraction of queries with exactly one compatible candidate

endpoints.name: fixed_execution_success
endpoints.role: secondary — exact verifier success for B=1/2/4/8

endpoints.name: adaptive_execution_success
endpoints.role: secondary — exact verifier success with early stopping

endpoints.name: adaptive_execution_work_fraction
endpoints.role: secondary — exact execution work normalized by exhaustive verification

endpoints.name: target_rank_index_only
endpoints.role: secondary — target rank in deterministic compatible-set order

held_constant: G-CASM-010 generator and pinned external generator commit
G-CASM-013 static evaluation-library construction and train/eval split rules
same five seeds, M levels and 32 tasks per seed/M
same deterministic task target selection and support-order hash as G-CASM-013
same exact graph executor and verifier
leakage_rules: Adaptive selection receives only the current compatible candidate indices, public candidate truth tables, and unobserved row indices.
Target identity and target index are not passed to the selector.
The target output for a row is exposed only after the selector commits to that row.
Rows not yet observed are unavailable as labels.
Final verifier rows are disjoint from probe rows.
No measured result is used to tune the selector or choose M, K or B.

primary_endpoint.success_definition: fixed-budget exact verifier finds at least one candidate matching all remaining verifier rows
primary_endpoint.estimate: mean across tasks within each seed, then paired adaptive_minus_fixed difference across five seeds

selector_definition.tie_break: maximize min(count(output=0), count(output=1)), then lowest row index
selector_definition.state_update: intersect compatible candidates with the newly observed row output

execution_accounting.adaptive_execution: may stop after first mismatch and after first passing candidate
execution_accounting.probe_observations: reported separately and never merged numerically with executor work

controls: exhaustive exact verification success is 1.0 for every query
target remains in the compatible set after every observation
probe decision cannot depend on target index
probe and verifier rows are disjoint
raw per-seed task data is retained

decision_rule.condition: Primary paired delta is positive with a seed-bootstrap interval not crossing zero.
decision_rule.licenses: evidence that adaptive target-identity-blind evidence acquisition improves fixed-evidence selective capability on the registered finite-domain workload.
decision_rule.does_not_license: learned probe selection, generic active-learning superiority, asymptotic retrieval, or multimodal capability.

decision_rule.condition: Adaptive ambiguity falls but capability does not improve.
decision_rule.licenses: candidate elimination is real but downstream candidate ordering or execution remains limiting.
decision_rule.does_not_license: failure of information acquisition as a mechanism.

decision_rule.condition: Adaptive ceiling fails to beat the frozen support order.
decision_rule.licenses: the registered finite-domain upper-bound strategy does not improve this workload at the fixed evidence budget.
decision_rule.does_not_license: impossibility of learned or representation-aware probing elsewhere.
